### Supporting basis
Zstandard offers distinct advantages for repeated text patterns like JSON field names due to its efficient dictionary compression and long-range match finder, even at level 3. While gzip level 6 provides solid compression, Zstandard’s architecture is optimized for high throughput with low CPU overhead on the compression side, crucial for your single-thread constraint. More importantly, Zstandard dramatically outperforms gzip in decompression speed, often achieving multi-gigabyte per second rates with minimal CPU usage. Since your workflow involves writing once but reading repeatedly, the slightly longer compression time of zstd is negligible compared to the cumulative savings in decompression latency. Empirical benchmarks consistently show that Zstandard level 3 yields comparable or better compression ratios than gzip level 6 while delivering 3-10x faster decompression. For 10 GB of logs with repetitive structure, Zstandard reduces I/O wait times during frequent reads, making it superior for practical performance where read frequency exceeds write frequency.

### Recommendation
I strongly recommend Zstandard at compression level 3. The primary driver is the asymmetric workload: you compress once but decompress repeatedly. Zstandard’s decompression speed is an order of magnitude faster than gzip’s, significantly reducing CPU and I/O load during log analysis or retrieval. While gzip level 6 might achieve a similar compressed size, its decompression bottleneck will hinder your repeated read operations. Zstandard level 3 strikes an optimal balance, offering near-optimal compression for repetitive JSON data without the excessive CPU penalty of higher levels. The single-thread compression speed of zstd level 3 is also competitive with gzip, ensuring the initial archive creation remains timely. By choosing Zstandard, you maximize throughput for the more frequent decompression tasks, leveraging its superior algorithmic efficiency for text-heavy, repetitive logs. This choice minimizes long-term operational costs associated with CPU usage during log access, providing a robust, high-performance solution for your archiving needs.<|im_end|>
